grammatica.evidence: Coinage 'fathers-forth'; compounds 'couple-colour','Fresh-firecoal chestnut-falls'; stress marks 'áll trádes'; dense asyndetic triples—'fold, fallow, and plough'; 'gear and tackle and trim'.

dialectica.evidence: Move from 'All things counter, original, spare, strange' / 'fickle, freckled' and antithetical pairs to 'He fathers-forth whose beauty is past change'—standard mutable-many→immutable-One doxological inference.

rhetorica.evidence: Chosen instances: brinded-cow skies, stippled trout rose-moles, firecoal chestnuts, finches' wings, pieced fold/fallow/plough, trades' gear; then abstract pairs; concrete→class→God→'Praise him' order.

arithmetica.evidence: Atomic claims: glory for dappled things; skies couple-colour as brinded cow; trout rose-moles in stipple; chestnut-falls firecoal; finches' wings; landscape plotted; all trades' gear; He fathers-forth; beauty past change; Praise him.

geometria.evidence: Title 'Pied Beauty'; two blocks (ll.1–6 catalog / ll.7–10 reflective); progressive indent levels; final 'Praise him.' isolated far right as orphan close.

musica.evidence: Alliterative stress-clusters ('Fresh-firecoal chestnut-falls; finches' wings'); antithetical pair cadence 'swift, slow; sweet, sour; adazzle, dim'; marked stresses; litany pace then snap close.

astronomia.evidence: Arc: open 'Glory be…dappled things' → concrete cascade → 'áll trádes' widen → abstract counter/fickle → freckled aporia → rapid pairs → 'beauty is past change' pivot → isolated 'Praise him.'

notes: Hopkins Pied Beauty; telos is the poem's explicit move; musica/grammatica carry original load; dialectica is traditional Christian inference under public devotional substrate.
